A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TWINGS study and complete supplementary Sections A-G. All 17 pages support comparison; pages 2-17 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original TWINGS evaluations on DTU, LLFF and Mip-NeRF360, including benchmark results, ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary analyses reported in v1.

M1.justification: The multi-view correspondence and triangulation procedure, TPS deformation, calibrated point sampling and training objective are identical in both versions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same sparse-view reconstruction tasks on DTU, LLFF and Mip-NeRF360. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and supplementary experiments. This includes the retained supplementary comparisons with MASt3R, NexusGS, Binocular3DGS, Dust-GS and SPARS3R.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and supplementary Section G retain identical splits, training-view counts, downsampling, evaluation metrics and training procedures, including the 10,000-step optimization budget.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 retains the same correspondence, initialization, deformation and sampling-radius ablations. Supplementary matcher, covisibility, point-cloud and view-selection analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-15 and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same TWINGS DTU 3-view PSNR of 21.52 and SSIM of 0.880 in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1-14, the TPS and triangulation formulations, and mathematical assumptions remain unchanged, including the known-camera-pose assumption in supplementary Section G.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient TPS-based initialization, geometric accuracy and sparse-view reconstruction quality. The added project-page pointer introduces no scientific claim.

C2.justification: The explanations of foreground/background coverage and diminishing benefits with increasing views remain identical. Section 6 and supplementary Sections C-D retain the same limitations concerning correspondence quality and reliable existing geometry.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page hyperlink at the end of the abstract. Implementation details, hardware, timings and hyperparameters are otherwise unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any new code or data release.

R1.justification: Related-work discussion, research positioning and all 47 reference entries are unchanged. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: A short project-page pointer is appended to the abstract, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose, terminology and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added link slightly reflows the abstract and first-page introduction, alongside the updated margin stamp. Figures, tables and the layout of pages 2-17 remain identical.

improvement.justification: The revision adds a convenient project-page pointer but leaves the method, evidence, explanations, limitations and full supplement unchanged. This small navigation benefit and accompanying first-page reflow do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
